1.reproduce_code:
---
# title: "Nav-fill + Panel-Tabset Bug Demo"
format: html
---

# Example of panel-tabset + nav-fill (broken in 1.3.x)
:::{.panel-tabset .nav-fill}

## Tab A

This is content for Tab A.

## Tab B

This is content for Tab B.
:::

---

# Workaround: reverse the class order (still works)

:::{.nav-fill}
:::{.panel-tabset}

## Tab A

Content for Tab A again.

## Tab B

Content for Tab B again.
:::
:::
1.explanation:
1. Save the above snippet as demo.qmd and run `quarto render demo.qmd --to html` (or `quarto preview`).  
2. In Quarto 1.2.x you will see both tabs equally filling the width.  
3. In Quarto 1.3.x (prerelease) the first example (panel-tabset + nav-fill) reverts to default Bootstrap sizing.  
4. The second example shows that if you wrap .panel-tabset inside a parent .nav-fill container, the tabs will again stretch to fill the container.  

This reproduces the change in behaviour between versions.
1.bug_scenario:
When you apply both the .panel-tabset and .nav-fill classes to the same container in Quarto 1.3.x, the tabs no longer expand to fill the full width of the container. In Quarto 1.2.x the two tabs would be forced to equal width and stretch across the container. In the prerelease (1.3.146) the .nav-fill class is effectively ignored and you see the default Bootstrap tab styling (tabs sized to text only). The attached screenshots show:  

– Quarto 1.2.335: two tabs each taking 50% of the width  
– Quarto 1.3.146: tabs sized to their labels
